sentences.text: Exploring a research collaboration on CLN3 disease (juvenile Batten disease)
We are writing to the Beyond Batten Disease Foundation, which supports families with juvenile Batten disease, and we would also welcome the views of BDFA and BDSRA.
CLN3 disease is linked to lysosomal storage, the build-up of material inside lysosomes.
People with CLN3 disease take part in the BDCRC natural history study and consortium, and in the DEM-CHILD natural history database, which is recruiting.
Another Natural History Study of Batten Disease was terminated, as was an optic-to-audio device study.
A Cellcept phase 2 trial is completed, a gene therapy trial is active but not recruiting, and a PLX-200 phase 2 study is not yet recruiting.
Miglustat is listed as in development, but we hold no results on it.
We would like to explore a jointly designed study on CLN3 disease, shaped with your community from the start: [study question], [design], [sites].
Any participation would follow informed consent and ethics approval, and we would share what we learn with your community.

sections.heading: What we would ask of you

sentences.text: Would you be open to a conversation about whether this idea is useful to the families you serve?
If so, we would value your view on how your community, registry or natural history work could take part, with proper consent and ethics approval.
We are not asking for any personal information about patients or families.
Could we arrange a short call at a time that suits you, perhaps [proposed dates]?
With thanks and warm regards, [researcher name], [institution].
